headline: Long-read DNA and RNA methods are benchmarked for SVs, isoforms, and m6A calling
label: Long Read Variant And Modification
summary: New benchmarks compare local assembly for SV calling, Kinnex RNA-seq for diagnosis, and Dorado m6A calling, while HARICOT assembles nanopore signals without basecalling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking and calibration of long-read analysis. One preprint compares five local-assembly consensus strategies for SV calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data and finds data-type-dependent performance. A Genome Medicine study evaluates PacBio Kinnex RNA-seq against short-read sequencing for Mendelian diagnosis in 50 individuals, with a new isoform pipeline. An eLife study benchmarks Dorado versions for direct-RNA m6A against GLORI and proposes stringent filtering and a best-practice workflow. HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling. GapCNV, TERRACE 2.0 and the Drosophila transposon-isoform study address CNV detection, circular RNA assembly and isoform diversity, and are adjacent to the long-read methods. The items do not show joint variant and modification calling.
